testsuite.name: com.zynergylabs.forager.app.data.backup.JournalBackupTest

testcase.name: a backup whose format version this build does not know is refused
two incoming regions get two different new ids
back up then Replace into an empty phone gives every journal table's rows and every photo file back, equal
a backup from schema 16 restores through the registered migration, gaining an empty path table
a failure after the rows are written and before the commit leaves the phone's rows and files exactly as they were
after a Replace a later download that arrives with the backup's old id cannot overwrite a restored row
a Merge of a backup into the phone that made it changes nothing at all, its regions included
a backup made with searches on the phone holds no cached_searches rows, and the phone keeps its searches
Merge keeps an entry's ref to a track that is on neither phone, with its saved path, and drops nothing
a snapshot that fails its integrity check is refused, and so is a zip with no manifest
Merge skips an incoming region that is the phone's own within half a metre, and rewrites the incoming references to the phone's region
Merge gives an incoming region a new id, negative so no future MapLibre id can meet it, and rewrites every reference
an archive entry the manifest does not list, or one that would land outside the scratch folder, is refused
Merge of an entry the phone already has keeps the phone's saved path and adds none of the backup's
Replace keeps a live photo file that shares a name with the backup's until the swap is done, and puts it back if the swap fails
Replace keeps a phone region the backup matches, drops one it does not, and gives an unmatched incoming region a new negative id
Merge still adds an incoming region that differs in name, in radius, or by two metres
told to ask, a backup with every photo readable is written whole
Merge of an older backup that holds searches leaves the phone's own searches exactly as they were
a backup from schema 15 restores through the registered migration, on a scratch copy
Replace keeps an entry's ref to a deleted track and its saved path, the path byte for byte
Replace deletes the phone's own journal data, planned trips included, and the photo files no restored row uses
Replace onto the phone that made the backup keeps its own regions, adds none, and points every reference at them
told to skip, a photo row whose file is missing is left out of the archive, counted, and the backup succeeds
an older backup's migration runs on a scratch copy and never on the live database
told to ask, a backup with an unreadable photo writes nothing to the sink and reports how many
the snapshot holds the write lock while it copies, so no writer can commit mid-copy
Merge adds what the phone lacks, skips an id it already has and keeps the phone's copy, and leaves no row dangling
a truncated zip is refused and leaves the phone untouched
a find that names a region the backup does not hold has that link cleared by a Replace, not left to meet a future id
every table in the schema is either journal data or explicitly excluded, and the specs match the schema
the snapshot inside a backup is a whole database that passes an integrity check and holds the phone's rows
Merge sets a link to NULL when its target is on neither phone, the rule the app already applies on a delete
Replace from an older backup that holds searches leaves the phone's own searches exactly as they were
Replace gives a restored region a fresh id, the same rule Merge uses, and rewrites every reference
a backup is a zip of the manifest first, the snapshot and the photos, and nothing else
Merge still drops a waypoint ref whose waypoint is gone, in the same entry that keeps its deleted track
a photo file that exists but cannot be read counts as unreadable
a backup that holds the same region twice, both matching the phone's one, adds nothing and keeps one reference per entry, in both modes
Replace drops an entry's region ref whose region the backup lacks, counts each, and logs it
a backup newer than the app is refused, with the reason logged, and the phone is untouched
a photo whose bytes do not match the manifest's hash is refused by name, and the phone is untouched
